turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start by telling me who decided that, and when.
Sorry, I'm a bit frazzled, it's report card week.
That's not Owen's problem, Hale. Who decided, and when?
You're the first parent this month who's actually listened to me. Thank you. I mean it.
Don't manage me, Hale. I've asked you twice now who entered that zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before you did.
I really needed that today. Can we just be kind to each other in here?
Kind would have been a phone call before the zero went in. I'm still waiting for an answer, Hale: who decided, and was Owen heard first?
